I am trying to find a reference for how straightening and unstraightening is constructed/done in this model. Recall that this is done in Higher Topos Theory (it is on this page)

It is important that the construction be native to simplicial categories rather than one which uses the concept of a Quillen equivalence.

content:
#2 Dean: the missuse of ‘simplicial category’ as a synonym for ‘simpllically enriched category’ predates Julie Bergner’s article as it was essentially already there in Dwyer and Kan’s work on simplicially enriched groupoids. I must admit to not fully understanding the straightening / unstraightening terminology but you might find the old papers by myself and Cordier, which is mentioned on the nLab page on homotopy coherent category theory to be of use. We tried to develop that theory directly but the combinatorics involved did get quite complex.

The fully developed theory of quasi-categories, or weak Kan complexes as they were then called, came along a few years later, and so rendered our techniques slightly obsolete.

To sketch the idea I am interested in, I believe this model has interesting benefits in terms of the construction of an internal universe. To do this, one considers the category of small simplicially enriched categories and regard it as enriched over the category of simplicial sets by identifying the compabitility condition on this simplicial set:

It is important that the internal universe operates by the theory of V-enriched categories and this is not something that other kinds of objects like algebras for operads have.

One question I am now interested in is, given a loop space Ω(X,x)\Omega(X,x)Ω(X,x), which is an algebra for an operad, is there a formula involving trees and/or necklaces which produces an equivalent A∞{}_{\infty}∞​-space but where in the new space the operation is a formal device involving trees/necklaces, in fact an associative one?

#4 I think I have developed enough intuition to try to prove this. I think I’ll leave a comment here for now and return if there is more interest.

An algebra for an (nonsymmetric) A∞A{}_{\infty}A∞​-operad such as the one constructed using endpoint preserving continuous functions from [0,1]\text{[0,1]}[0,1] to $\text{[0,1] \vee_{0,1} \cdots \text{[0,1]}}$ can be reinterpreted using PROPs as a functor enriched over topological spaces or locales, and after thinking this should be the seed of the idea I read more about homotopy Kan extensions.

More specifically, I recalled how there is an enriched PROP-category PROP(A)\text{PROP}(A)PROP(A) corresponding to the operad AAA, which is a category enriched over topological spaces. An operad-algebra is an enriched functor. This is mentioned a 2.4 here.

Such an operad and algebra pair can be CW-replaced. Doing this to Ω(X,x)\Omega (X,x)Ω(X,x) produces maps of

CW(A∞(n))×cellularCW(Ω(X,x))×cellular⋯×cellularCW(Ω(X,x))→CW(Ω(X,x)) \text{CW}(A_{\infty}(n)) \times_{\text{cellular}} \text{CW}(\Omega(X,x)) \times_{\text{cellular}} \cdots \times_{\text{cellular}} \text{CW}(\Omega (X,x)) \rightarrow \text{CW}(\Omega(X,x)) CW(A∞​(n))×cellular​CW(Ω(X,x))×cellular​⋯×cellular​CW(Ω(X,x))→CW(Ω(X,x))

The terminal CW-A∞{}_{\infty}∞​-operad 1CW-A∞-operad\text{1}_{\text{CW-A}_{\infty}\text{-operad}}1CW-A∞​-operad​ is the one in which each CW-complex of nnn-ary operations is the terminal CW-complex, which has a single cell in each dimension. The operadic composition maps are cellular.

content:
#6 Unclear to me what your question is in the end. Maybe you want to know:

  • How are A∞A_{\infty}A∞​-groups rectified to topological groups?

(You speak of “amortizing” A∞A_\inftyA∞​-groups. Maybe an autocorrect error?)

One answer to this question is the following:

  1. A∞A_\inftyA∞​-groups are equivalently loop spaces under concatenation of loops (the “May recognition theorem”, cf. here).

  2. Loop spaces under concatenation of loops are equivalently presented by the Kan loop simplicial group-construction.

  3. Topological realization of simplicial groups yields topological groups, since it preserves products (see here).

#11 I am motivated to some extent that way, but the differences in particular models matter for what I am proposing.

My goal is to describe the cleanest possible counterpart to straightening and unstraightening in the context of categories enriched over topological spaces.

I proposed above that rectification of an A∞{}_{\infty}∞​-group can be regarded as a homotopy Kan extension, but I also had in mind the classical theorem that G//GG//GG//G is contractible for a topological group GGG, which specifically features the continuous functions

μ:Δn×[0,1]→Δn \mu : \Delta^n \times \text{[0,1]} \rightarrow \Delta^n μ:Δn×[0,1]→Δn

sending a weighted average ∑i=0naiei∈Δn\sum_{i = 0}^n a_i e_i \in \Delta^n∑i=0n​ai​ei​∈Δn to

a0⋅e0+t⋅(∑i=1naiei−a0⋅e0) a_0 \cdot e_0 + t \cdot \left( \sum_{i =1}^n a_i e_i - a_0 \cdot e_0 \right) a0​⋅e0​+t⋅(i=1∑n​ai​ei​−a0​⋅e0​)

where

Δn={(x0,...,xn)∈[0,1]:∑i=0nxi=1},ei=(δi,0,...,δi,n)∈Δn \Delta^n = \left\{ (x_0,...,x_n) \in \text{[0,1]} : \sum_{i =0}^n x_i = 1 \right\}, e_i = (\delta_{i,0}, ..., \delta_{i,n}) \in \Delta^n Δn={(x0​,...,xn​)∈[0,1]:i=0∑n​xi​=1},ei​=(δi,0​,...,δi,n​)∈Δn

This argument does not work for all algebras for an operad, only rectified ones.

I also recently learned about what is known as Thomason’s theorem, which in its higher form can be found here:

A. Mazel-Gee, {{On the Grothendieck construction for $\infty$-categories}}, ''Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra'' '''223''' (2019), no. 11, pp. 4602–4651. \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.03525}{arXiv:1510.03525}. \href{https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpaa.2019.02.007}{doi:10.1016/j.jpaa.2019.02.007}.

where a generalization of Thomason’s theorem occurs in 2.1 as:

Proposition 2.1 For any C→FCat∞\mathcal{C} \stackrel{F}{\rightarrow} \mathcal{Cat}_{\infty}C→FCat∞​, the Grothendieck construction computes its homotopy colimit when considered as a diagram in (Cat∞)Th(\mathcal{Cat}_{\infty})_{\mathrm{Th}}(Cat∞​)Th​, i.e.

Gr(F)gpd≃colim(C→FCat∞→(−)gpdS) \mathrm{Gr}(F)^{\mathrm{gpd}} \simeq \text{colim} \left( \mathcal{C} \stackrel{F}{\rightarrow} \mathcal{Cat}_{\infty} \stackrel{(-)^{\text{gpd} }}{\rightarrow } \mathcal{S} \right) Gr(F)gpd≃colim(C→FCat∞​→(−)gpdS)

In this context, groupoid completion can be defined for rectified objects using the recognition principle for them and by defining realization as:

∐n∈N,(X0,...,Xn)∈Obj(C)n+1HomC(X0,X1)×⋯×HomC(Xn−1,Xn)×Δn/∼ \coprod_{n \in \mathbb{N}, (X_0,...,X_n) \in \text{Obj}(C)^{n+1}} \text{Hom}_C(X_0,X_1) \times \cdots \times \text{Hom}_C(X_{n-1},X_{n}) \times \Delta^n \big/ \sim n∈N,(X0​,...,Xn​)∈Obj(C)n+1∐​HomC​(X0​,X1​)×⋯×HomC​(Xn−1​,Xn​)×Δn/∼

This can be compared directly with how the classical argument does not work for operadic structures since the simplices “allow for insertion of identies in words”.
